elements.problem: Section heading; it justifies the Emergency level used by both priority rules.
The 'No' branch (does not respond to voice or physical stimulation) is encoded as Unresponsive, which gives Emergency.
evidence: Emergency: emergency patient unresponsive, pulseless or not breathing :: (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Unresponsive" "finding"))
(task "Check for emergency patient airway, breathing and circulation signs") due_to :: (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Unresponsive" "finding"))

elements.problem: The No branch is captured under p16-e64d521e (Unresponsive).

Emergency: emergency patient unresponsive, pulseless or not breathing :: (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Cardiac arrest" "disorder"))

elements.problem: 'If no pulse' is already covered by Absent pulse.

Airway obstruction is encoded as Respiratory obstruction, Snoring, Gurgling and Noisy respiration, and gives Emergency. 'Neck injury suspected, use jaw-thrust' is a management modifier, out of scope by design.
evidence: Emergency: emergency patient with airway, breathing, circulation or consciousness compromise :: (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Respiratory obstruction" "disorder")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Snoring" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Gurgling" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Noisy respiration" "finding"))

elements.problem: Both parts (difficulty breathing; SpO2 < 94%) are standalone Emergency triggers. They are correct as criteria, but see rule-level problem 1 on anchoring.
evidence: Emergency: emergency patient with airway, breathing, circulation or consciousness compromise :: (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Difficulty breathing" "finding"))
Emergency: emergency patient with airway, breathing, circulation or consciousness compromise :: (< (measurement (snomed_concept "Hemoglobin saturation with oxygen" "observable entity") %) 94)

elements.problem: Pulse < 50 AND (SBP < 90 OR DBP < 60 OR decreased consciousness OR chest pain OR acute heart failure, also given as leg swelling AND (orthopnea OR dyspnea on exertion), per footnote 3). The logic matches. Reading BP < 90/60 as SBP<90 OR DBP<60 is the usual one. The atropine dose is management.
evidence: Emergency: emergency patient with airway, breathing, circulation or consciousness compromise :: (and (< (measurement (snomed_concept "Pulse, function" "observable entity") bpm) 50) (or (< SBP 90) (< DBP 60) Decreased level of consciousness, Chest pain, Acute heart failure, (and Swelling of lower limb (or Orthopnea, Dyspnea on exertion))))

elements.problem: GCS component scale. The components can't be represented individually; only the total (≤ 8) is used.

evidence: Emergency: emergency patient with airway, breathing, circulation or consciousness compromise :: (< (measurement (snomed_concept "Respiratory rate" "observable entity") bpm) 9)

Emergency: emergency patient with airway, breathing, circulation or consciousness compromise :: (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Blue lips" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Blue tongue" "finding"))

elements.scope_reason: Ambiguous parse of 'If shock/SBP < 80, pulse ≥ 100 or heavy bleeding'. It could be three independent triggers (as encoded) or 'shock, i.e. SBP<80 with pulse ≥ 100'. The fluid-choice sub-branch (known heart problem / severe infection) and the repeats are management.
elements.problem: Encoded as four independent Emergency triggers: active Shock, SBP<80, pulse ≥ 100 and severe bleeding. Taking pulse ≥ 100 alone as an Emergency trigger is the literal reading, but it over-triggers (see rule-level problem 1). Heavy bleeding uses Bleeding + Severe; the warning-sign form is Bleeding + Uncontrolled.
evidence: Emergency: emergency patient with airway, breathing, circulation or consciousness compromise :: (active_condition (snomed_concept "Shock" "disorder"))
Emergency: emergency patient with airway, breathing, circulation or consciousness compromise :: (< (measurement (snomed_concept "Systolic blood pressure" "observable entity") mmHg) 80)
Emergency: emergency patient with airway, breathing, circulation or consciousness compromise :: (>= (measurement (snomed_concept "Pulse, function" "observable entity") bpm) 100)

Emergency: emergency patient with airway, breathing, circulation or consciousness compromise :: (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Bleeding" "finding") (qualifier (snomed_concept "Severe (severity modifier)" "qualifier value")))

elements.problem: Intubation criteria; every trigger finding is already an Emergency trigger.

Probable Tension pneumothorax = sudden dyspnea AND (unilateral hyperresonance OR unilateral decreased breath sounds OR unilateral chest pain) AND displaced trachea. This is a defensible reading of the comma list, and it feeds the Emergency rule through active_condition. The conjunction is strict: a deviated trachea is a late sign.
evidence: Diagnose probable tension pneumothorax (emergency patient) :: (and (clinical_finding Dyspnea + Sudden onset) (or Hyperresonance+Unilateral, Decreased breath sounds+Unilateral, Chest pain+Unilateral) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Trachea displaced" "disorder")))
Emergency: emergency patient with airway, breathing, circulation or consciousness compromise :: (active_condition (snomed_concept "Tension pneumothorax" "disorder"))

elements.problem: GCS ≤ 8 is encoded as the six discrete findings 'Glasgow coma scale, 3'…'8', which give Emergency. This only works if the system records GCS as those findings; there is no measurement form for a total score.
evidence: Emergency: emergency patient with airway, breathing, circulation or consciousness compromise :: (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Glasgow coma scale, 3" "finding")) … (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Glasgow coma scale, 8" "finding"))

elements.scope_reason: Footnotes 1 (palliative CPR) and 2 (jaw-thrust technique) are figure_or_note; the two footnote-3s carry logic.
elements.problem: Footnote 3a (acute heart failure = leg swelling + dyspnea worse lying down or with effort) is encoded correctly in the bradycardia branch. Footnote 3b (shock likely) is encoded as probable Shock = SBP<80 AND pulse≥100 AND RR>30 AND (Clouded consciousness OR Acute confusion OR Restlessness) AND Asthenia. All concepts are right, but requiring all five criteria makes the rule almost never fire (see rule-level problems). 'Clouded consciousness' is a looser match for 'confusion' than Acute confusion.
evidence: Diagnose probable shock (emergency patient) :: (and (< SBP 80) (>= Pulse 100) (> Respiratory rate 30) (or Clouded consciousness, Acute confusion, Restlessness) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Asthenia" "finding")))

rule_level_problems.rule: Emergency: emergency patient with airway, breathing, circulation or consciousness compromise
rule_level_problems.problem: The Emergency priority rule has no presenting-complaint anchor. The house standard says (and <presenting complaint> (or …)); here every item is a standalone trigger for any adult. Routine vitals or common symptoms alone give Emergency: pulse ≥ 100, SpO2 < 94, SBP < 80, Difficulty breathing. Any febrile patient with pulse 100 is classed Emergency. On the page these thresholds are management cues inside an already-identified emergency patient, and 'SBP < 80, pulse ≥ 100' is plausibly a definition of shock rather than two separate triggers.

rule_level_problems.rule: (task "Check for emergency patient airway, breathing and circulation signs")
rule_level_problems.problem: The task's due_to fires the full emergency check_for list on isolated vitals such as pulse ≥ 100, RR > 30 or SpO2 < 94. This is the same over-triggering as problem 1, on the task side.

The footnote's comma list is encoded as an AND of five criteria (SBP<80, pulse≥100, RR>30, confusion/restlessness, weakness). That is very restrictive, so the rule will rarely fire. In practice it adds nothing, because the priority rule already fires on SBP<80 or pulse≥100 alone. An any-N or (and SBP<80 (or …)) reading is arguably closer to the intent.

rule_level_problems.rule: Emergency: emergency patient with airway, breathing, circulation or consciousness compromise
rule_level_problems.problem: GCS ≤ 8 depends on the discrete 'Glasgow coma scale, N' findings being recorded, and nothing measures a total GCS. If GCS isn't recorded in that form, the criterion is dead.

rule_level_problems.rule: Emergency: emergency patient with airway, breathing, circulation or consciousness compromise
rule_level_problems.problem: Heavy bleeding is encoded as Bleeding + Severe; the existing warning sign uses Bleeding + Uncontrolled, so the two may not connect.

summary: Every logical element of the page is captured with valid SNOMED concepts and the right thresholds: unresponsive, no pulse, gasping, airway obstruction, the breathing, bradycardia and shock criteria, GCS ≤ 8 and tension pneumothorax likely. The most consequential problem is that the Emergency priority rule has no emergency-presentation anchor, so isolated pulse ≥ 100, SpO2 < 94, SBP < 80 or difficulty breathing makes any adult an Emergency. Second, the probable Shock rule ANDs all five footnote criteria and will rarely fire.
